beats.narration_text: Every transformer layer does the same four things in the same order, and stacking enough of them gives you every modern language model. I'm Anjana — here's what one token actually sees on its way through one layer.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Hello, Anjana'; ask types itself
runningText 'opening one layer…'
output lines resolve: 'attention gathers context' / 'feed-forward processes it' / 'residual and layer norm hold it together'

props.command: I keep hearing that a transformer is "just attention plus a feed-forward network," but I've never seen what one layer actually does to a single word. Can you walk one token through one layer, step by step?
output: residual and layer norm hold it together

beats.narration_text: Step one. Self-attention. The token "revenue" needs to understand its role in the sentence. It creates three vectors from itself: a query, a key, and a value. The query asks "what should I pay attention to?" Every other token in the sentence also has a key. The query compares against every key and computes a score. High score means high relevance. "Revenue" scores high against "growth" and "moderate" because they directly affect its meaning. It scores low against "we" and "to" because they add no context. The scores become weights. The weighted sum of all values produces a new, context-aware representation of "revenue." The word has not changed. But now it knows what surrounds it.

show.event: inside the layer: 'revenue' center stage, the other five tokens in a row
three vectors split out of 'revenue' — gold Q ('What should I attend to?'), blue K, green V; the other tokens show dimmer K and V
the gold query reaches every key; scores land on each connection — growth 0.42, moderate 0.31, expect 0.15, we 0.07, to 0.05
the scores are shown summing to 1.00 — softmax
the value vectors scale by their weights and flow back into 'revenue'
'revenue' glows differently — it has absorbed context; label: 'Same word. New meaning. Context-aware.'

beats.narration_text: Step two. The feed-forward network. Attention told "revenue" what to look at. Now the feed-forward network decides what to do with that information. It is two linear transformations with a non-linearity in between. The vector expands to a higher dimension, passes through an activation function that introduces non-linearity, then compresses back down. This is where the model transforms raw attention patterns into useful features. Attention gathers context. The feed-forward network processes it.

show.event: the context-aware 'revenue' vector enters a Feed-Forward Network box as a narrow color strip
the strip stretches to four times its width — 'Expand: d_model → 4× d_model'
it passes through a wave-shaped GELU gate; some cells brighten, others go dark
it compresses back to its original width — same size, transformed
the token exits with a different glow; label: 'Attention gathers. Feed-forward processes.'

beats.narration_text: Two more operations hold everything together. Residual connections. Before attention and before the feed-forward step, the original input was saved. After each operation, the original is added back to the result. This means the model can never completely forget what the token started as. If the layer learns nothing useful, the residual ensures the token passes through unchanged. No damage done. Layer normalization runs after each addition. It rescales the values so they stay in a stable range. Without it, values drift higher and higher through twelve layers and the model breaks. Residual connections protect the signal. Layer norm keeps the numbers in check. Together they are why you can stack twelve, twenty-four, or ninety-six layers and the model still trains.

show.event: a side-view flow diagram; the token enters from the left and the path splits — main through the attention block, a curved bypass around it
the two paths merge at a '+' node — 'Original + transformed = protected'
brief flash: attention learns nothing, the bypass carries the token through unchanged
a Layer Norm box; the vector strip's extreme values visibly settle into a stable range
a drift warning: values climbing layer after layer without norm
the same residual + norm pattern repeats around the feed-forward block
the full structure reads: Input → Attention → Add & Norm → FFN → Add & Norm → Output

beats.narration_text: Four operations. Attention gathers context. Feed-forward processes it. Residual connections protect the signal. Layer norm keeps it stable. Stack twelve of these and you have BERT. Stack ninety-six and you have GPT. Same four steps, repeated. That is a transformer.

show.event: the expanded layer collapses back into its block and rejoins the stack — microscope out
the four operations tick off beside the stack as they are named
on 'twelve' twelve blocks glow — 'BERT'
on 'ninety-six' the stack extends dramatically — 'GPT'
title lands: What Happens Inside a Transformer Layer / Four operations. One building block.
